feedback: Written before this candidate has raced; no outcome is stated for it. Evidence from iteration 2 (the last race): widening to seven sensors at 0.02 m spacing with a 16 mm footprint cut oval progress from 0.47 to 0.23 and lowered oscillation from 0.28 to 0.13, while max_error stayed at about 0.062 m on the oval. The robot became smoother but covered less track, so a wider, blurrier signal seems to under-respond on bends. For this candidate, the controller is unchanged from iteration 1 (kp 2.5, kd 0.30, ki 0, base_speed 1.5, last_direction, weights [-2,-1,0,1,2]), so the race result depends only on your footprint change. The integration point to watch is that 8 mm footprints still overlap the 25 mm tape across the offsets that matter, so no line-loss dead zone is expected at the 0.025 m spacing. Change the next design by what the race shows. If oval progress rises above 0.47 and max_error stays near 0.06 m, keep the 8 mm footprint and narrow the sensor spread or raise turn authority. If steering_oscillation rises above about 0.28 while max_error stays at or above 0.06 m, the sharper signal is adding jitter, so the drivetrain or the controller damping needs to change rather than the sensors. If line_loss_events increase above the iteration-1 value of 0.3, the signal has too little overlap at the edges and the array spread should widen slightly.
requested_changes: If oval progress stays at or above 0.47 but max_error is still at or above 0.06 m with steering_oscillation below about 0.3, set mass to 0.7 kg (from 0.6). Iteration 1 showed max_error of 0.064 to 0.066 m on the oval and s-bend with small rms_error, so the excursion is a bend overshoot that more yaw inertia should damp.

If steering_oscillation rises above about 0.3 (iteration 1 reached 0.28 on the oval) and rms_error rises with it, keep sensor_size at 0.008 and set wheel_track to 0.12 m (from 0.10 m). Iteration 0 with a 0.12 m track showed lower oval oscillation (0.085), so this trades some turn authority for damping.

If oval progress falls below 0.47 with the 8 mm footprint, the sharper signal is not the bottleneck; set sensor_size back to 0.012 m (the iteration-1 value) and set wheel_radius to 0.04 m (from 0.035 m). Iteration 1 showed oval progress was limited by speed (0.47 of the course), and the 3.0 s limit needs about 1.5 m/s average speed.
